This program encompasses the preservation of the existing paved national roads through the following sub-programs: Preventive Maintenance; Rehabilitation/ Reconstruction/Upgrading of damaged paved national roads; Rehabilitation/Reconstruction of National Roads with slips, slope collapse, and landslide; construction, upgrading/rehabilitation of drainage along national roads.</td><td style="text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;">36,094,823,000</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Preventive Maintenance</td><td style="text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;">36,094,823,000</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Preventive maintenance is a sub-program under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to preserve and prolong the lifespan of national roads. This program is typically carried out on roads that are in fair to poor condition, with the primary objective of preventing and delaying further deterioration to a state where extensive rehabilitation is necessary. Preventive maintenance aims to prevent and delay the deterioration of national roads to a bad condition where ultimately rehabilitation is required, which typically involves Asphalt Overlay, Asphalt Overlay with Correction, and Concrete Reblocking. Asphalt Overlay is done on roads in fair condition. It involves the application of an additional layer of asphalt, that covers imperfections in existing asphalt or concrete. It is commonly applied to pavement that has minor damage to the light cracking, mild deterioration, or slightly sunken areas. The process of overlaying asphalt commonly includes a leveling out of the old asphalt pavement, ensuring a smooth, even surface on which to add additional layers. Asphalt Overlay with Correction is done on roads in poor condition. It involves the repair of short intermittent damaged sections before applying asphalt overlay. For concrete roads, the most common type of corrective maintenance is a combination of concrete pavement restoration (CPR) in terms of the replacement of intermittent shattered slabs and asphalt overlay. Concrete reblocking is done on national roads in poor condition which involves selective reblocking or replacement of intermittent shattered slabs in bad condition. Process aims to improve the pavement's load-bearing capacity, reduce the risk of potholes, and enhance the pavement's durability and</td><td style="text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;">14,395,583,000</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Preventive Maintenance - Primary Roads</td><td style="text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;">12,353,654,000</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">National Capital Region</td><td style="text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;">12,333,081,000</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Central Office</td><td style="text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;">12,333,081,000</td></tr></table>

Eligibility for later classification as a national road is determined by a feasibility study and the functional classification criteria set by DPWH. This is also achieved through a range of activities such as road widening, the construction of bypasses and diversion roads, the construction of missing links/new roads, the construction of flyovers, interchanges, underpasses, long-span bridges, off-carriageway improvement, and the paving of unpaved roads.The program includes several sub-programs aimed at achieving its objectives. These sub-programs include: Road Widening; Construction of By-Passes and Diversion Roads; Construction of Missing Links/ New Roads; Construction of Flyovers/ Interchanges/ Underpasses/ Long Span Bridges; Off-Carriageway Improvement; Paving of Unpaved Roads</td><td rowspan="2">18,113,243,000</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Road Widening\nThis involves widening the existing road pavement to accommodate more lanes to ease traffic congestion, improve traffic flow, and increase road capacity.
